## generic_demo_transfer_gen1

**Reproduced teaching ambiguity — the purportedly unique in-grid transform is
not always unique.** At generator SHA-256
`5c2062bbe59a1eb7dde94638f977b89edd6b578394003dae30f99707adc0af36`,
seed 10, difficulty `easy`, training pair 1 contains this demonstrated mask
relation:

```text
X = 4000   Y = 0004
    0044       4400
    4400       0044
    0004       4000
```

Both library transform 2 (left-right flip) and transform 3 (up-down flip) map
`X` to `Y` in the allowed bidirectional demonstration test. On the generated
query mask they disagree:

```text
left-right: 0200  up-down: 2200
            0200           2200
            0022           0020
            0022           0020
```

The generator accepts this because `_unique_f` checks only that the intended
transform is the **first** match (`hits[0] == f_id`), not that there is exactly
one match. The Racket program likewise uses `find-first`, so its label is
well-defined by library order, but the visible demonstration does not teach
that ordering and supports two different query answers. Full masks, candidate
outputs, seed/split identity, source hash, and embedded-program hash are in
`checks/audit/generic_demo_transfer_gen1/ambiguity.json`.

This input is in the actual documented generator domain because it was emitted
by `generate_task`; it is not a hand-constructed out-of-domain case. The
per-puzzle `arcpuzzles apply` command does not support generic generators, so no
Racket-apply receipt could be produced for this target; the ambiguity itself is
independent of execution parity because both candidates fit the visible demo
exactly. No patch was made.

## generic_demo_transfer_gen1

**Reproduced teaching ambiguity: the purportedly unique demonstrated transform is not unique.** At generator SHA-256 `5c2062bbe59a1eb7dde94638f977b89edd6b578394003dae30f99707adc0af36`, seed 10, difficulty `easy`, training pair 1 is emitted directly by `generate_task`. Both transform 2 (left/right flip) and transform 3 (up/down flip) satisfy the generator's bidirectional demonstration relation, but they produce different outputs for the query mask.

The current `_unique_f` implementation returns true when the intended transform is merely `hits[0]`; it does not require `len(hits) == 1`. The visible lesson therefore supports two incompatible query answers even though the embedded program deterministically chooses the first by library order. Full masks, boxes, candidate outputs, generator hash, and program hash are in `checks/audit/generic_demo_transfer_gen1/ambiguity-current.json`; rerun with `checks/audit/generic_demo_transfer_gen1/reproduce_ambiguity.py`.

The pair belongs to the documented generator domain because it was emitted without filtering or hand construction. The generic generator does not expose the per-puzzle `arcpuzzles apply` route, so there is no Racket-apply receipt; the ambiguity is established before execution because both candidates fit the visible demo exactly and disagree on the query. No patch was made.
